body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Friday, October 2, and the biggest political story in California runs straight through Kern County — Republican Steve Hilton's long-shot bid for governor, which 23ABC reports faces a 4.6-million-voter registration gap. Closer to home, the Riverview Marketplace project takes another step toward approval, and a new state law targets social media's grip on kids. Expect a hot one: a high near 100°, no active weather alerts, and no fires reported in the county.

## The Kern Overnight

It was a night of pursuits, pole strikes, and fire calls across Kern County, according to preliminary emergency dispatch reports.

In Bakersfield, officers with helicopter support chased suspects who fled on foot across a property. The search drew air units overhead before the situation was resolved. Details remain preliminary and unconfirmed by an official source.

Fire crews also responded to a fire in Bakersfield around 9:25 p.m., followed minutes later by a structure fire reported on Cranbrook Avenue at about 9:27 p.m. In eastern Kern, crews worked a pair of vehicles that struck power poles — the kind of crash that can knock out electricity for surrounding blocks and tie up a roadway while crews make repairs.

As always, these early dispatch reports are just the first word, not the last. Names, exact locations, and outcomes will come from official sources as the day develops. What we can say this morning is that it was a busy overnight shift across the county, with no confirmed reports of serious injuries in the incidents described.

## Today's weather

It's 66° at Meadows Field as of this morning, according to the National Weather Service — a comfortable start before the heat settles in.

Expect a high near 100° today, with a low around 69° tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no active fires are reported. Air quality readings were not available at the time of this brief.

If you're headed out this afternoon, plan for genuine valley heat: water, shade, and a little patience go a long way. The cool morning won't last, so get the errands done early if you can.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that Republican Steve Hilton faces steep odds in his bid for California governor, with mail ballots set to arrive at homes in early October.** Hilton, a former Fox News commentator, is running against Democrat Xavier Becerra in a state that hasn't elected a Republican to statewide office in two decades. Registered Democrats outnumber Republicans by roughly 4.6 million voters, and President Trump's endorsement — while helpful with the base — is widely unpopular outside it. GOP consultant Mike Murphy told the Associated Press the math is "very hard." For Kern County Republicans, it's a reminder that even a friendly local electorate can't overcome a two-to-one statewide gap.

**According to KGET 17, two of the three candidates for Kern's Board of Education met on the debate stage, and the conversation stayed notably amicable.** The exchange gave voters a look at where the candidates stand ahead of the election. School board races rarely draw big headlines, but they shape decisions that touch every family in the county — budgets, curriculum, and how local schools are run. With ballots arriving soon, this is the kind of down-ballot contest worth a few minutes of your attention.

**KGET 17 also reports that the Riverview Marketplace project moved one step closer to approval, with the Bakersfield City Council set to consider its environmental impact report.** The EIR is a required checkpoint before the project can move forward, and it's the stage where traffic, noise, and environmental concerns typically get aired. For residents near the proposed site, this is the moment to weigh in. The council's review will determine whether the project keeps its momentum or faces delays.

**23ABC reports that California has enacted what experts call the nation's strongest law protecting children from social media addiction.** Gov. Gavin Newsom signed Assembly Bill 1709, a bipartisan measure by Assemblymember Josh Lowenthal that strips platforms of autoplay and algorithmically personalized feeds for users under 16. For one Bakersfield family, the issue wasn't abstract: Citlali Soto, a student at Independence High School, said Instagram and TikTok once consumed three to four hours of her day before her father cut them off when she was 12 or 13. Five years later, she told 23ABC she has no desire to go back. Her father said the law would have made that difficult decision easier.

**Bakersfield police have arrested a 29-year-old Arvin man on multiple felony charges, including kidnapping and aggravated sexual assault of a minor, 23ABC reports.** Antonio Rafael Gomez Martinez was arrested Sept. 14 and booked into the Lerdo Pre-Trial Facility without bail, with a court appearance scheduled for Nov. 3. Police say an 11-year-old Bakersfield girl was abducted in early September near the area of MLK Park and Union, then dropped off near her home the following day. Detective Bijan Gharib said surveillance footage and Flock camera data helped identify the suspect's vehicle. It's a case that has shaken the neighborhood, and one that shows how camera networks are increasingly central to local investigations.

**KGET 17 reports that 71 years after his death, the "James Dean Memorial Highway" is now official.** The designation honors the actor whose brief, blazing career made him a permanent fixture of American film — and whose story is woven into California's cultural memory. For Kern County, where Dean's legacy still draws visitors and film buffs, the highway marker is a small but lasting tribute.

**Bakersfield police are searching for a woman accused of breaking into the Salvation Army, according to Bakersfield Now.** The investigation is ongoing, and anyone with information should contact the department. Nonprofits like the Salvation Army serve some of the county's most vulnerable residents, so a break-in there hits the community twice — once in lost resources and once in the sense of security for the people who rely on it.

## Something good

The Norris School District is set to build a new elementary school in Shafter, a project that marks a real step forward in expanding local school capacity. Shafter has been growing, and new classrooms mean fewer crowded campuses and shorter commutes for families. It's the kind of quiet, unglamorous investment that pays off for decades — and it's worth a smile this morning.

## Coming up this week

The Bakersfield City Council meets twice on Wednesday, October 7 — first at 3:30 p.m. and again at 5:15 p.m. The Riverview Marketplace environmental impact report is expected to be part of the council's business, so if you have thoughts on that project, Wednesday is the day to show up or send a comment. Both sessions are open to the public.

Also on the calendar: the Housing and Community Development Committee meets Thursday, October 8 at noon, and the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets Friday, October 9 at noon. These are the smaller, less crowded meetings where a lot of the groundwork gets done — housing policy and neighborhood safety both shape daily life in Bakersfield, and public input carries real weight at this level.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate ahead. "Cults & Classics: Young Frankenstein" screens Monday, October 5. The NB RIDAZ "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off" tour rolls in Friday, October 9, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. "United We Dance: Festival Energy. All Night." takes over the Fox on Friday, October 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour lands Saturday, October 17. If you've been meaning to catch a show downtown, October is the month.

That's your Friday, Bakersfield. Stay cool out there — and if you're heading to the council meeting Wednesday, we'll see you there.

top.title: Steve Hilton faces steep odds in bid for California governor after 20-year GOP drought
